newsitem.title: USA: Tenneco sets note tender offer prices.
newsitem.headline: Tenneco sets note tender offer prices.

text.p: Tenneco Inc said it has set the final prices for repurchasing its debt in a tender offer, as part of the restructuring of the company.
The purchase price will be based on a premium over U.S. Treasury securities with comparable maturities, Tenneco said.

In November, the company announced a refinancing of $3.53 billion in debt. The company is spinning off its Newport News Shipbuilding unit and merging its energy business with El Paso Natural Gas Co, Tenneco said.
Tenneco will focus on the automotive parts, packaging and administrative services businesses, the company said.
The tender offer for the notes is set to expire 1700 EST on December 10, 1996, unless extended, the company said.

Among the issues, $500 million of Tenneco's 10 percent Notes due August 1, 1998 will have a purchase price of 106.455 percent of par and $400 million of six percent debentures due December 15, 2011 at 92.920 percent of par, the company said. The purchase prices do not include accrued interest and are based on a settlement date of Friday, December 13, 1996, Tenneco said.
